FI-mock-bisht.title: Yuvan Bisht
FI-mock-bisht.background: Yuvan Bisht, a fixed-income portfolio manager, is reviewing investments in his fund. Bisht values a convertible bond issued one year ago by Doredum at a par value of $100. Each bond can be converted to 25 shares of Doredum common stock. The current share price is $3.80. A comparable option-free bond of the same maturity is valued at $105. Based on Doredum's strong operating performance, Bisht expects its share price will reach $8.00 in one year. Next, Bisht values a 3% default-free annual coupon bond with a 2-year maturity. The bond is putable at par ($100) at the end of Year 1. He estimates the binomial interest rate tree shown in Exhibit 1, assuming interest rate volatility of 15% and that branching from each node to a high state and to a low state occurs with equal probability. Bisht considers a scenario in which the assumed level of interest rate volatility increases from 15% to 25%. He considers the impact of this scenario on the value of the putable bond. Bisht analyzes the effects of an interest rate scenario in which there is a non-parallel shift in the yield curve, where the only change in the curve is a 30 bp increase in the 2-year benchmark. He considers the most appropriate measure to evaluate the putable bond's sensitivity to this scenario.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Binomial interest rate tree (15% volatility; rates cited in the solutions)

EQ-mock-albertson.title: David Albertson
EQ-mock-albertson.background: David Albertson is an equity analyst at an investment bank. He is preparing updated research reports on two companies, Xita Incorporated and Garc Company. Xita Incorporated: In Albertson's previous report on Xita, the stock had a forward P/E ratio of 14.9 and a trailing P/E ratio of 15.7. He considers a likely explanation for the difference in the P/E ratios. Albertson indicates in his updated report that Xita's profits are cyclical. Using the data for the past four years in Exhibit 1, he computes Xita's normalized EPS based on the average ROE method. He determines that Year 1 through Year 4 (the most recent year) constitutes a full business cycle. Garc Company: Albertson next reviews Garc, which operates in a previously mature industry that now has high growth potential due to a recent technological innovation. Garc's debt-to-equity ratio is significantly higher than the average of its competitors. Garc spent heavily on advertising to create and maintain its brand, which is an important asset. The company is favored by many investors because its dividend payout ratio is the highest in its industry. Albertson considers several potential metrics to use in valuing Garc. During the past year, Garc's share price rose from $27.95 to $31.05 per share and the company paid an annual dividend of $1.24 per share. Over the same period, the market index rose from 550.40 to 602.21 and had an average dividend yield of 3.4%. Albertson computes Garc's relative strength compared to the index, which is a common technical indicator.

FSA-mock-traske.title: Susan Traske
FSA-mock-traske.background: Susan Traske is an analyst specializing in financial institutions. She is evaluating Sigmar, a large US-based commercial bank. Traske uses the CAMELS (capital adequacy, asset quality, management, earnings, liquidity, and sensitivity) approach in her evaluation of Sigmar. As part of this analysis, she examines Sigmar's liquidity ratios and notes that the bank's net stable funding ratio has increased steadily over the past three years. She then investigates which components of the ratio explain this trend. Traske reviews Sigmar's employee compensation policy and notes that a large restricted stock grant vested during the current year. The share price on the settlement date was greater than the share price on the grant date. Recognizing that Sigmar prepares its financial statements in accordance with US GAAP, Traske considers the effect of the vested grant on Sigmar's income tax expense for the current year. Sigmar sponsors a defined benefit pension plan for employees. Sigmar's pension disclosure for the most recent year is shown in Exhibit 1 (amounts in $ millions). Traske notes that there was no amortization of past service costs, no amortization of actuarial gains or losses, and no amortization of differences between actual and expected return on plan assets. Finally, Traske compares the overall efficiency of the underwriting operations of three property and casualty insurance companies based on the information in Exhibit 2.

EQ-mock-laver.title: Shawn Laver
EQ-mock-laver.background: Shawn Laver, a buy-side analyst, is evaluating three companies: Globac, Waltun, and Dentoc. Laver first values Globac, a natural resources company that has significant iron ore reserves. Due to its weak growth prospects, Globac has generated negative earnings and negative operating cash flows in recent years. This trend appears likely to continue for the foreseeable future. Next, Laver computes Waltun's FCFF using the most recent fiscal year data (in $ millions) provided in Exhibit 1. Waltun has a tax rate of 30% and its financial statements are prepared under US GAAP. Laver computes Dentoc's FCFE for the most recent year to be $750 million. He believes the company will have annual growth of 12% for each of the next three years, followed by a decline to the industry-average growth rate of 4%. Laver assumes a required rate of return on equity of 10% and a WACC of 9%. Using a two-stage model, Laver estimates the intrinsic value of Dentoc's common equity. Six months later, Laver revises his FCFE projections of Dentoc to incorporate the impact of several financial decisions approved by the company's board: Decision 1: Dentoc will pay a cash dividend of $2 per share to its common shareholders. Decision 2: Dentoc will buy back 1 million shares of its own common stock. Decision 3: Dentoc will modify its capital structure by increasing its level of debt by 5%.

FSA-mock-clerc.title: Jules Clerc
FSA-mock-clerc.background: Jules Clerc is an equity analyst at an asset management firm. Clerc is evaluating Lonza Credit Inc., a bank that prepares its financial statements under IFRS and has a 31 December year end. The bank is subject to the Basel III regulatory framework. Lonza offers a defined benefit pension plan to its employees. To evaluate the pension plan, Clerc uses the data (in EUR millions) for the most recent year in Exhibit 1. Based on the data from Exhibit 1, Clerc calculates the pension plan's funded status for the most recent year as part of her valuation of Lonza. On 1 January of the current year, Lonza granted 4 million stock options to employees. The options vest 3 years after the grant date and expire 6 years after the grant date. The fair value per option was EUR 1.8 on the grant date. Lonza is planning to issue 5 million restricted stock units (RSUs) to its employees. The RSUs will vest two years after issuance. Clerc uses a profitability measure – free cash flow as a percentage of revenues – to analyze Lonza. He considers how this measure would be affected immediately after the issuance of the RSUs. Clerc uses the CAMELS (capital adequacy, asset quality, management, earnings, liquidity, and sensitivity) approach to evaluate Lonza. Clerc gathers Lonza's liquidity ratios over the past two years in Exhibit 2.

EQ-mock-kassam.title: Julia Kassam
EQ-mock-kassam.background: Julia Kassam is a portfolio manager who is reviewing public and private equity investments for her clients. Erebor Limited: Kassam values a manufacturing company, Erebor, using the EV/EBIDTA ratio. The company's last reported EBIDTA is $90 million. Kassam collects relevant financial information (in $ millions) in Exhibit 1. Biotechnology Sector: One of Kassam’s clients wants to increase their exposure to growth stocks in the biotechnology sector. The sector currently has a median P/E ratio of 10.7 and is expected to grow at 7%. Kassam uses the PEG ratio to identify overvalued stocks from her list of three selected biotechnology stocks in Exhibit 2. Altair Corp.: Kassam evaluates the stock of Altair, which is a recently listed, high growth, biotechnology company. She is considering a stable market-based multiple to value the stock and does not want to make any adjustments to the reported financial statements. After reviewing recent analyst reports, Kassam notices that Altair has internally generated brands that are not shown as intangible assets on Altair's balance sheet. Further, she notes that certain discretionary accounting decisions about expenses have led to an inaccurate representation of Altair's economic performance. Becq Inc.: Kassam values Becq, a small private company, using the excess earnings method. Relevant financial information is shown in Exhibit 3.

FI-mock-plessinger.title: Sandra Plessinger
FI-mock-plessinger.background: Sandra Plessinger is evaluating several bonds for the fixed-income portfolios she manages. She first considers the following 2-year, default-free bonds with embedded options: Bond A is a 5% annual pay coupon bond and is callable at par ($100) at the end of year 1. Bond B is a 5% annual pay coupon bond and is putable at par ($100) at the end of year 1. To analyze these bonds, Plessinger creates a binomial interest rate tree using the rates in Exhibit 1, assuming an interest rate volatility of 20%, with branching from each node to a high state and a low state occurring with equal probability. Plessinger also considers the effective convexity of Bond B. Plessinger next evaluates a 3-year maturity, callable investment-grade corporate bond. She computes an OAS of 51 bps using the same binomial interest rate tree in Exhibit 1. Plessinger considers the impact on the bond's OAS under a scenario where the bond's price is unchanged and interest rate volatility increases from 20% to 25%. Finally, still using the binomial interest rate tree in Exhibit 1, Plessinger analyzes a 3-year, default-free capped floating rate bond with a par value of $100. The bond pays an annual coupon equal to the 1-year reference rate, is set in arrears, and is capped at 5.0%.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Binomial interest rate tree (20% volatility; 1-year rates cited in the solutions)

EQ-mock-mccormick.title: Terry McCormick
EQ-mock-mccormick.background: Terry McCormick is a US-equity analyst working for a large wealth management firm. He is currently working on DCF valuations of various publicly traded firms, which report under the US GAAP. Firm A: McCormick wants to identify the most appropriate approach to value Firm A, which consistently had positive FCFE during the past decade. Management is about to start an aggressive growth strategy primarily financed with debt. McCormick expects highly fluctuating amounts of net borrowing for the next three years. McCormick also expects annual earnings growth rate to fluctuate between 25% and 35% during the next three years before it gradually declines to long-run sustainable rate of 2%. Firm B: McCormick calculates FCFE for the most recent fiscal year and gathers the selected financial information in Exhibit 1 (in $ millions). Firm C: McCormick reviews his FCFE valuation model for Firm C. Firm C's management has just announced that they will issue new common stock during the next year. McCormick evaluates the potential effect of this change on next year's FCFE forecast. Firm D: McCormick estimates the intrinsic value of Firm E's common equity using the FCFF approach. McCormick calculates the present value of the firm's future FCFF as $800 million. McCormick estimates that $75 million of the firm's cash holdings is not necessary to generate operating cash flows. Current market values of the firm's debt and preferred stock are $250 million and $150 million respectively.

FSA-mock-tay.title: Alex Tay
FSA-mock-tay.background: Alex Tay is an analyst researching Buttery Ranch International. Buttery is a Hong Kong SAR-based retail company reporting under IFRS. Buttery and its subsidiaries have fiscal years ending on 31 December. Buttery's functional and presentation currency is the USD. Tay collects components of Buttery's net sales growth from various markets of the most recent year in Exhibit 1. Creamy Meadows is a subsidiary of Buttery. Creamy began operations in Indonesia on 1 January of the most recent year and uses the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) as its functional currency. Buttery uses the temporal method to translate Creamy's financial results. For the most recent year, Creamy had a net monetary liability and the IDR strengthened against the USD. Tay believes that the translation method may distort the financial and operating measures of the international subsidiary. To verify this, Tay compares Creamy's translated ratios to the ratios calculated under the local currency by using the exchange rates of the most recent year in Exhibit 2. Finally, Tay analyzes another subsidiary of Buttery, Dairy Barn. Dairy uses the local currency of its home market as its functional currency. Buttery used the current rate method to translate Dairy's financial statements in the most recent year. Dairy's home market has been experiencing high inflation and Tay expects it to be classified as a hyperinflationary economy beginning in the current year.

FI-mock-xiaoli.title: Xiao Li
FI-mock-xiaoli.background: Xiao Li is a private wealth manager who focuses on fixed income markets. He is reviewing the term structure of interest rates for his domestic market. Li observes that lender and borrower preferences strongly influence yield curve shape, especially for longer-term maturities. For example, Li has detected that the curve has a persistent dip at the 10-year maturity, and that investors in 10-year bonds are not willing to shift to 8- or 12-year bonds even when yields in those maturities are relatively high. Li reviews Exhibit 1, which contains current shorter-term government bond spot rates. Using the spot curve, Li computes forward rates. He then forecasts that in three years the 2-year spot rate will equal 2.20%, the current 2-year spot rate, but that the remainder of the spot rate curve will be consistent with current forward rates. Li evaluates what his forecast implies about the valuation of a 5-year zero-coupon bond today. Li is assisting Client A to select an appropriate investment strategy, who has a 2-year investment horizon. The client expects the yield curve to remain unchanged over the 2-year horizon. Li recommends implementing a ride the yield curve strategy using government bonds for Client A. Li studies the characteristics and effects of yield curve volatility. He uses the 3.25% monthly standard deviation of the 15-year government-bond yield to estimate an annual yield volatility of 11.26%. Li also calculates key rate durations for various maturities. He concludes that the higher key rate durations associated with longer-term rates leads to higher long-term annualized term structure volatility.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Current shorter-term government bond spot rates

FSA-mock-mcandrew.title: Carol McAndrew
FSA-mock-mcandrew.background: Carol McAndrew, an equity analyst, specializes in evaluating manufacturing companies. McAndrew is currently evaluating Acme Industries, a large, diversified manufacturing company that reports under IFRS. During a recent conference call, Acme management disclosed its intent to raise EUR 40 million to fund new investments by borrowing against Acme's EUR 50 million of receivables. Management indicated that it is evaluating two different options to accomplish this objective: Option 1: Borrow directly against the receivables of EUR 50 million; Option 2: Create a special purpose entity (SPE), invest EUR 10 million in the SPE, have the SPE borrow EUR 40 million, and then use the funds to purchase EUR 50 million of receivables from Acme. McAndrew considers the potential impact of these options on Acme's consolidated debt-to-assets ratio, assuming that Acme will be able to influence the financial and operating policy of the SPE, and will be expected to absorb any losses that the SPE may incur. Next, McAndrew examines whether there are any accounting warning signs related to the overstatement of Acme's net income. After reviewing Acme's financial reports and industry data for the most recent year, McAndrew makes the following observations: Observation 1: Receivables growth is lower than revenue growth. Observation 2: Management compensation is largely tied to financial results. Observation 3: Depreciable lives of Acme's fixed assets are shorter than those of industry peers. McAndrew also reviews Acme's Beneish M-scores and Altman Z-scores for the past three years and notes that both scores have steadily declined during this time. Finally, after making any necessary adjustments, McAndrew uses the following data (in EUR millions) to compute Acme's cash-flow-based accruals ratio for the most recent year: Net income: 7,050; Operating cash flow: 9,826; Investing cash flow: –8,410; Financing cash flow: 5,390; Average net operating assets: 45,894.

EQ-mock-bala.title: Ulu Bala
EQ-mock-bala.background: Ulu Bala, an analyst for ValEwe Consulting, has been hired to provide valuations for several firm clients. Firm A is a rapidly growing automotive parts distributor that has asked Bala to provide an estimated fair value of its common stock. Bala selects the appropriate valuation model based on the following information about Firm A: The firm's dividend payout ratio has been stable over the last 10 years and is expected to remain stable, regardless of future profitability. Planned expansion into new markets will require significant annual capital expenditures, which will result in dividends exceeding free cash flow to equity. Compared with peers, the firm has an aggressive policy with respect to reported earnings, as well as a lower quality of accounting disclosure. Firm B is a regional utilities provider. Firm B’s current stock price is $19.00 and Bala uses the dividend discount model to value the stock. In Exhibit 1, Bala forecasts Firm B’s earnings for the next three years. He assumes a required return on equity of 8% and a 60% retention ratio. By the end of Year 3, Bala expects Firm B’s stock price to be $21.50. ValEwe's approach is to consider a stock to be fairly valued if its price is within 2% of its estimated fair value. Firm C is a power generation company. Bala forecasts that Firm C's earnings will grow by 8% per year and the cost of equity will remain at 11% for the foreseeable future. Using the DuPont model and the information in Exhibit 2, Bala estimates Firm C's sustainable growth rate. Bala then values Firm C's stock using the Gordon growth model. He evaluates the sensitivity of the stock price from the model under a scenario where both the forecasted cost of equity and the earnings growth rate increase by 50 bps.

FI-mock-kehoe.title: Cathryn Kehoe
FI-mock-kehoe.background: Cathryn Kehoe is the senior credit analyst for the State Teachers' Pension Fund. She is conducting credit analysis of an ABS held in the fund's portfolio. The ABS is backed by a large number of short-term credit card receivables that are homogeneous. Each receivable is small relative to the total value of the pool. Kehoe proposes purchasing a 3-year corporate bond issued by Valisker, Inc. The YTM on the Valisker bond is 2.60%. The bond has a credit rating of AA and a modified duration of 2.82. The relevant portion of a 1-year corporate transition matrix, along with corresponding credit spreads, is presented in Exhibit 1. In the matrix, for example, the probability of an AAA-rated bond becoming an A-rated bond at the end of the year is 1.2%. The fund owns $5 million of a 7-year senior unsecured bond issued by Gonk Industries. Kehoe recommends the fund buy $5 million of credit protection on Gonk using a 5-year CDS. The CDS has a 5-year senior unsecured bond as its reference obligation. Summary data for the CDS are presented in Exhibit 2. Two months later, a major accounting scandal is uncovered at Gonk and the firm quickly files for bankruptcy. Gonk has three series of bonds outstanding: 3-year subordinated unsecured bonds trading at 20% of par value; 5-year senior unsecured bonds trading at 40% of par value; 7-year senior unsecured bonds trading at 30% of par value.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. 1-year corporate transition matrix (entries in %) and credit spreads

QM-silva.title: Alice Silva -- Construction Spending Time Series
QM-silva.background: Alice Silva is a quantitative analyst focusing on the real estate sector. Silva studies the extent to which private construction spending is affected by public construction spending. She collects data (in $ millions) on total private (PRIV) and public (PUBL) construction spending for the last 363 months and log-transforms both time series. To determine whether the two log-transformed time series are cointegrated, Silva tests the following null hypotheses: Null Hypothesis 1: ln(PRIVt) has a unit root. Null Hypothesis 2: ln(PUBLt) has a unit root. Null Hypothesis 3: The error term of the linear regression between ln(PRIVt) and ln(PUBLt) has a unit root. Silva forecasts future private construction spending. She estimates an autoregressive model of order 1 (AR(1)), where dln(PRIVt) = ln(PRIVt) - ln(PRIVt-1), using the estimates in Exhibit 1 to determine the mean-reverting level of dln(PRIVt). Next, Silva estimates an AR(1) model for public construction spending, where dln(PUBLt) = ln(PUBLt) - ln(PUBLt-1). She calculates the residuals (e) and squared residuals (e^2) of the AR(1) model and estimates two linear regressions: Residual Regression 1: et = a0 + a1*et-1 + ut; Residual Regression 2: et^2 = a0 + a1*et-1^2 + ut. The t-statistic for the slope coefficients (a1) is 0.70 for Residual Regression 1 and 2.94 for Residual Regression 2. The relevant critical value for these tests is 1.97. Finally, Silva develops a sentiment indicator for the real estate market. She obtains text data from real estate listings and classifies each listing as 'hot,' 'medium,' or 'cold' based on how quickly the property sold. After preparing and wrangling the unstructured data, she performs feature selection. She wants to remove noise features and only select the tokens that tend to occur more often in a particular class of text.

QM-moreno.title: Sebastian Moreno -- ML, Logistic Regression and Model Fit
QM-moreno.background: Sebastian Moreno is an analyst analyzing probabilities of default for bond issuers and the drivers of ROE. He is tasked with a project to classify bond issuers by their probability of default within the next 12 months. He gathers financial and accounting metrics for 1,000 issuers and observes that the issuers are not linearly separable. He compares non-linear support vector machine (SVM), unconstrained classification and regression tree (CART), and SVM with soft margin classification. He wants an algorithm that addresses non-linear separability and is not prone to overfitting. Moreno also creates Model 1, a logistic regression using two factors, profit margin (PROFIT) and leverage ratio (LEVER), to predict probability of default. The binary dependent variable is 1 for companies that defaulted within the subsequent 12 months and 0 otherwise. Using Exhibit 1, he calculates the predicted probability of default for the average distressed company, which has PROFIT = -2.0 and LEVER = 3.0. To analyze drivers of ROE for software companies, Moreno compares two linear regressions. Model 2 uses profit margin (PROFIT) and interest coverage (COVER). Model 3 extends Model 2 by adding a third factor, the quick ratio (QUICK). He compares the R-squared and adjusted R-squared of the two models; results for Model 3 are in Exhibit 2. Finally, Moreno tests if last-12-month sales (SALES) are a good predictor of ROE with Model 4: ROEi = b0 + b1*SALESi + ei. A plot of the regression residuals against SALES shows the variance of residuals increasing as SALES increase.

QM-aoun.title: Danny Aoun -- ML Metrics and Time-Series Forecasting
QM-aoun.background: Danny Aoun is an equity portfolio manager developing sentiment indicators for forecasting stock price movements. He gathers textual data from the internet, extracts raw content, and trains machine-learning models for sentiment prediction. Each text item is labelled positive or negative sentiment. Aoun is more concerned about the models producing false negatives than false positives. He computes selected performance metrics for three models using confusion matrices (Exhibit 1). Aoun then applies his models to two semiconductor stocks, Bytewave and Circuitcraft. For Bytewave, Aoun estimates a first-order autoregressive model (AR(1)) on the stock price and concludes the model exhibits autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity with ARCH(1) errors. For Circuitcraft, Aoun predicts growth in quarterly sales using 13 years of quarterly data, running a regression on the first difference of quarterly sales growth in an AR(2) model. After reviewing the first-differenced data, he determines the mean and variance are constant over time and concludes the time series does not have a unit root. Historical quarterly sales growth: Sales Growth50 = 18.9%, Sales Growth49 = 2.0%, Sales Growth48 = -11.5%. The critical value for the t-statistic is 2.0 at the 5% significance level. Exhibit 2 shows results from this regression.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2. First-differenced AR(2) regression for Circuitcraft

QM-cambo.title: Jan Cambo -- Model Selection, Clustering and Diagnostics
QM-cambo.background: Jan Cambo is a data analyst at a US asset management firm managing index funds and ETFs. Cambo wants to identify the macroeconomic factors that best explain the returns on the local stock market index, the SPX500. Based on Exhibit 1 he evaluates how many factors to incorporate and selects the best-fitting model. Cambo is launching a new ETF. To minimize trading and rebalancing costs he limits the number of stocks included, using a machine-learning algorithm to combine index stocks into groups based on the co-movement similarity of their returns, then selecting the five most liquid stocks from each group. Cambo estimates a regression of monthly excess returns (RET) against three factors: the market excess return (MRKT), the difference in returns between value and growth stocks (HML), and the difference in returns between small- and large-cap stocks (SMB), with output in Exhibit 2. He then estimates RET for an out-of-sample observation, assuming MRKT is 0.9%, the return on value stocks is 1.2%, on growth stocks is 3.8%, on small-cap stocks is 4.0%, and on large-cap stocks is 2.2%. Cambo checks his regression against the multiple-regression assumptions and calculates the Breusch-Pagan (BP) test statistic to be 5.8. Critical values are in Exhibit 3.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2. Multiple regression of RET on MRKT, HML, SMB

QM-lin.title: John Lin -- Data Cleansing, Classification and Unit-Root Testing
QM-lin.background: John Lin is an analyst at GFE Co. building a model with structured financial data. Alex, the CEO, already uses some of Lin's machine-learning methods to screen loan applicants. Exhibit 1 presents a small sample of the raw dataset before cleansing. Lin uses logistic regression to train the model: defaulting loans are Class 1, non-defaulting loans are Class 0. After tuning, a threshold p-value of 0.6 (for Class 1) is used to predict the outcome for each loan application (Exhibit 2). Lin believes the previous loan application affects the current one, so he uses model A, a first-order autoregressive model AR(1). He determines the coefficient of the first lag is significantly different from zero, and calculates the autocorrelations of the residuals up to four lags, finding that only the residual autocorrelation at the second lag is significantly different from zero. Lin then conducts a Dickey-Fuller test for model A using the regression Xt - Xt-1 = b0 + g1*Xt-1 + et, with results in Exhibit 3.

DER-wu.title: Julie Wu -- BSM Delta Hedging and Binomial Option Pricing
DER-wu.background: Julie Wu is a US-based hedge fund manager. To value the options in her fund she uses both the Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) and binomial option pricing models. Wu sells 10 call option contracts on a non-dividend-paying stock, Skyview Corporation, at the value determined by the BSM model, and considers delta-hedging the position using Skyview shares. Each call option contract is for 100 shares. Wu collects the information in Exhibit 1 for a call option on Skyview. Wu next considers an American-style put option on Wilbo Corporation that matures in two years. She values it with a two-period binomial option pricing model and collects the relevant information in Exhibit 2. Wilbo does not pay dividends.

DER-bueden.title: Bueden -- Swaps, Currency Swaps and Forward Arbitrage
DER-bueden.background: Bueden manages a family office's EUR-denominated portfolio and uses swaps and forwards. He holds a two-year equity swap on a EUR 1,000,000 notional that receives the return on an equity index and pays a fixed rate of 2.3%. Since initiation the fixed rate has moved to 1.8% and the equity index is trading at 104.8 (from a base of 100). Bueden determines the no-arbitrage value of the equity swap using the present-value factors in Exhibit 1. Over the next year Bueden expects AUD cash inflows from an Australian equity portfolio and hedges the currency exposure with a fixed-for-fixed currency swap with a notional of AUD 16 million. The AUD/EUR spot exchange rate is 1.60 AUD per EUR and notional amounts are exchanged at initiation and maturity. The interest rate on the EUR leg is 1.8%. Bueden calculates the interest rate on the AUD leg that results in a contract value of zero at initiation using the present-value factors in Exhibit 2 (sum of PV factors = 3.94889). Bueden next identifies an arbitrage in shares of Reyab: a forward contract on Reyab is trading at EUR 63.25 while the theoretical arbitrage-free price is EUR 63.65. Finally, Bueden evaluates a 9-month forward on Furblag entered at a price of EUR 123. Six months after initiation, the dividend has been paid and Furblag shares trade at EUR 131. The annually compounded interest rate is 1.6%.

DER-knizek.title: Ondrej Knizek -- Interest Rate Options, FRAs and Bond Forwards
DER-knizek.background: Ondrej Knizek is a portfolio manager at a European asset management firm; his portfolio includes fixed income and currency derivatives. Knizek believes the market is underestimating potential interest rate hikes in Hungary and is considering buying a 2-year European-style call option on the periodically compounded one-year Hungarian forint (HUF) spot interest rate, valued with a two-period binomial model. Exhibit 1 shows the 1-year discount factor and the fair value of the options for the respective up and down moves at Time Step 1 (c+ and c-), assuming a risk-neutral probability of 50%. Knizek holds US Treasuries maturing in one month and wants to use a forward rate agreement (FRA) to lock in the 6-month US interest rate at the time the bonds mature, referring to the annualized reference rates in Exhibit 2. Knizek then observes an arbitrage in a Polish government bond whose 6-month forward price is below fair value; as the first step he purchases 100 bond forward contracts at a price of 109.30 (percent of par), each with a notional of 100,000 PLN. Three months later he calculates the fair value of the forward position: the current forward contract bid price is 108.15 and the annualized three-month interest rate is 0.65%.

DER-carter.title: Dylan Carter -- FRA Settlement, Futures and Equity Swaps
DER-carter.background: Dylan Carter, chief risk officer at Nexus Capital Asset Management Group, discusses derivatives strategies with his assistant Savage Olaf. First they settle an FRA contract. In 60 days Nexus expects to make a bank deposit of $10,000,000 for 90 days at 90-day MRR set 60 days from today. Nexus is concerned about a decrease in interest rates and enters a $10,000,000 notional FRA priced at 0.65%. After 60 days, 90-day MRR is 0.55%. Next they price a Treasury bond futures contract. Carter provides a Treasury bond with face value $100,000, a 7% semiannual coupon, 15 years to maturity, priced at $156,000, no accrued interest, yielding 2.5%. The futures contract expires in 8 months and the annualized risk-free rate is 1.5%. The conversion factor for this bond is 1.098. Carter holds a long equity forward on QuantumByte Technologies (QBT) with a remaining maturity of two months; the continuously compounded dividend yield is 0.8%, the current stock price is $82, and the continuously compounded annual interest rate is 0.32%. Carter entered a one-year equity swap 270 days ago that receives the return on the SCI 300 Index and pays a fixed annual rate of 4.8% on a notional of CNY 50,000,000, with quarterly payments. At initiation the index was 3,250; today it is 3,738. Exhibit 1 provides present value factors based on the current term structure.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Present value factors (current term structure)

DER-goldsworthy.title: Connor Goldsworthy -- Binomial, BSM and Delta Hedging
DER-goldsworthy.background: Connor Goldsworthy is an analyst for a multi-strategy hedge fund that uses derivatives to take directional and volatility bets on stocks and indices. The continuously compounded risk-free return is 3%. Goldsworthy values options on Sunrise, a non-dividend-paying stock with a current price of $25, and Sunset, a dividend-paying stock with a current price of $50 (Exhibit 1). Both Sunrise and Sunset satisfy the specific assumptions of the Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) model regarding their stochastic process, liquidity, trading, and absence of market frictions and arbitrage opportunities. Goldsworthy assesses the extent to which the BSM model could provide a valid alternative to the binomial tree analysis. To value the call option on Sunset, Goldsworthy builds a two-step binomial tree with a risk-neutral probability of an up move of 51.11%. The payoffs at the three nodes at the second step are c++ = $30.125, c+- = $2, c-- = $0. For the Sunrise 1-year option, Goldsworthy uses a binomial tree with up-factor 1.32 and down-factor 0.76. Finally, Goldsworthy wants to determine the potential return of delta-hedged positions on Moonlight stock, buying one of the options in Exhibit 2 and delta-hedging with Moonlight shares. He observes that Moonlight's stock price often jumps and considers the consequences for delta-hedging effectiveness.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Options on Sunrise and Sunset

ALT-pasco.title: Martin Pasco -- Commodities and Hedge Fund Strategies
ALT-pasco.background: Martin Pasco is an analyst with the Hekla University Endowment, evaluating opportunities to increase the alternative investments allocation. Pasco considers Fund 1, a commodity managed futures fund. Current price data for the largest exposures in Fund 1 are in Exhibit 1. Pasco reviews a previous cocoa trade for Fund 1: at inception the fund took a fully collateralized long position in a 3-month futures contract at $3,294. Three months later the entire position was rolled into a new 3-month futures contract; at that time the price of the initial futures contract was $3,285 and the price of the new 3-month futures contract was $3,260. The collateral earned an annualized return of 5.0% during the three months. Pasco also evaluates equity hedge fund strategies. He reviews Fund 2, an event-driven hedge fund with a merger arbitrage trade between Acquirer Company (AC) and Target Company (TC). AC has offered to buy TC in a stock-for-stock deal with an offer ratio of one share of AC for three shares of TC. AC traded at $39 before the announcement and fell to $35 after; TC traded at $10 before and rose to $11 after. After the announcement the hedge fund bought 30,000 shares of TC at $11 and sold 10,000 shares of AC at $35. Pasco is also evaluating a single fund that combines multiple strategies versus multiple single-strategy funds: Option 1 is a fund of funds; Option 2 is a multi-strategy fund.

ALT-friso.title: Martina Friso -- Real Estate Indexes, REITs and NAV
ALT-friso.background: Martina Friso is a portfolio manager at a pension fund that currently invests in domestic equities and bonds and is considering adding real estate. Friso uses mean-variance optimization to determine the appropriate allocation to real estate. She considers using either a transaction-based or an appraisal-based real estate index to assess the volatility of real estate returns, the estimation of the Sharpe ratio, and the correlation of returns with the existing portfolio, and chooses the appraisal-based index. Friso compares two publicly traded real estate companies in the retail sector: Perpetua Properties, a REIT, and Rainfall Real Estate, a real estate operating company (REOC). Both manage retail shopping centers and plan to grow their portfolios by acquiring undervalued assets. The key objective of Friso's analysis of Perpetua Properties is to evaluate its sustainable dividend-paying capacity, considering FFO, adjusted FFO (AFFO), and net income. Finally, Friso assesses Perpetua Properties' NAV per share using the data in Exhibit 1. Perpetua Properties has 100 million shares outstanding.

ALT-chang.title: Sophia Chang -- Liquid Alternatives and Hedge Fund Strategies
ALT-chang.background: Sophia Chang is the head of alternative investments at a defined benefit pension plan and is considering an investment in liquid alternatives. She identifies two requirements the investment must meet: Requirement 1 -- have a lower incentive fee than the industry average for traditional hedge funds; Requirement 2 -- allow more frequent redemptions than traditional hedge funds. Chang is also evaluating hedge funds as potential additions and identifies three strategies, considering their returns, leverage, and liquidity: Strategy 1 -- multi-strategy funds; Strategy 2 -- fund of funds; Strategy 3 -- long/short equity funds. Chang identifies a skillful manager who deploys Strategy 3 and determines which factor is the primary source of outperformance: market timing, stock selection, or use of leverage. The pension plan has an objective to limit drawdowns, and Chang considers which individual hedge fund strategy would best meet that objective when combined with the plan's stock and bond portfolio.

ALT-baldwin.title: Cara Baldwin -- REIT Valuation and Commodity Futures
ALT-baldwin.background: Cara Baldwin is a portfolio manager at Paleo Asset Management, a US firm serving retired individuals through managed accounts. Paleo has decided to increase the long-term allocation to real estate and commodities across all portfolios. Baldwin collects information on two REITs in Exhibit 1 (all data in USD millions except per-share data). To value the REIT shares she uses price to adjusted funds from operations per share (P/AFFOPS), price to funds from operations per share (P/FFOPS), and net asset value per share (NAVPS). Paleo's policy states that if a REIT's market value lies within +/-5% of the estimated intrinsic value relative to its sub-sector average, the security is considered fairly valued. Baldwin is also considering commodities to hedge against increasing inflation and analyzes coffee futures (Exhibit 2). Year 0 is the current year and Year 1 is next year; prices are in USD.

ECON-podlasky.title: Andrew Podlasky -- Economic Growth Models
ECON-podlasky.background: Andrew Podlasky is an analyst at an investment management firm reviewing growth prospects under different economic models for Country A and Country B. First, Podlasky reviews the macroeconomic data in Exhibit 1 to determine the current steady-state growth rates and potential GDP growth rates of both countries. Country A, currently operating at its steady state of growth, has announced its intention to remove trade barriers on capital investments; as a result, Podlasky concludes that the country's economic growth rate per capita will increase permanently. For Country B, Podlasky estimates that the output gap (the difference between the real growth rate in potential GDP and short-term real GDP growth) has widened by 0.8 percentage points as a result of a 0.2% higher estimated real growth rate in potential GDP and a 0.6% lower estimate of real growth in short-term GDP.

ECON-bernard.title: Joanne Bernard -- Currency Arbitrage, Parity and Crises
ECON-bernard.background: Joanne Bernard is a currency trader for a US-based hedge fund. She reviews interbank bid-offer quotes in Exhibit 1 (USD/EUR is the number of USD per 1 EUR; JPY/USD is the number of JPY per 1 USD). Bernard determines if an arbitrage profit is possible based on a dealer's bid/offer rate quote of 119.38/119.40 in JPY/EUR. The hedge fund considers hedging a New Zealand dollar (NZD) 1,000,000 coupon payment it will receive in six months. Bernard calculates the 6-month forward USD/NZD exchange rate implied by covered interest rate parity, where the 6-month annualized MRR in the US is 0.50%, the 6-month annualized MRR in New Zealand is 1.00%, and the spot mid-market quote for USD/NZD is 0.6808. Bernard next considers a 1-year carry trade that borrows USD and invests in the Brazilian real (BRL): the spot mid-market quote for BRL/USD is 5.1300, the 1-year MRR in the US is 1.00%, the 1-year MRR in Brazil is 9.75%, and the BRL/USD exchange rate in one year is 5.2000. Finally, Bernard is concerned about a currency crisis in emerging market Country B and notes three conditions: Condition 1 -- a slight decline of foreign investment in its equity market; Condition 2 -- broad money growth and a decline in the ratio of M2 to bank reserves; Condition 3 -- a sizable decline in the ratio of FX reserve holdings to average daily FX turnover in their domestic currency.

ECON-smith.title: Richard Smith -- Growth Accounting and Convergence
ECON-smith.background: Richard Smith is the chief economist at BMT Consulting conducting a training program on economic growth, with new analyst teams presenting on various topics. Smith begins with a framework explaining the percentage change in stock market value as the sum of the percentage change in GDP, the percentage change in the ratio of earnings to GDP, and the percentage change in the price-to-earnings multiple. Smith shows that the growth accounting equation decomposes the percentage change in output into components attributable to capital, labor, and technology. Team Blue is asked to calculate the economy's potential growth rate using the growth accounting method with: growth rate of capital = 2.0%, growth rate of labor = 0.5%, growth rate of total factor productivity = 1.0%, share of capital in GDP = 30%. Team Green discusses how investment in physical capital, human capital, and technological development affects growth, presenting three points: Point 1 -- since technology results in an upward shift in the production function, the relationship between economic growth and R&D spending is positive in the short run; Point 2 -- total factor productivity reflects the state of technology and can be measured by the contribution of capital deepening plus the growth rates of labor productivity; Point 3 -- although long-term sustainable growth cannot rely on pure capital deepening, the impact of investment spending on available capital depends on the existing physical capital stock. Team Purple investigates whether the per capita income of a developing country should converge toward that of developed countries, reviewing the saving rate, population growth rate, the shape of the production function, and the externalities associated with human capital, and concludes that the externalities associated with human capital is the most important determinant in predicting convergence. Smith concludes that opening up the economy should increase the rate at which countries' capital-to-labor ratios converge, and Team Orange provides three descriptions of the dynamic adjustment process: Description 1 -- the growth in the capital-exporting countries will be above the steady state; Description 2 -- developed countries will tend to run trade deficits as they export capital; Description 3 -- the rate of return on investments will be lower in countries with high capital-to-labor ratios.

ECON-suzy.title: Suzy -- Forward Mark-to-Market and Growth Accounting
ECON-suzy.background: Suzy, a portfolio manager at a UK hedge fund, sold GBP 10 million forward against the USD at an all-in forward price of 1.2465 (USD/GBP), while the spot exchange rate is 1.25. Two months before the settlement date, Suzy wants to mark this forward position to market. The relevant spot rate, forward points, and Libor are given in Exhibit 1 (USD/GBP quoted as bid/offer; forward points in pips). The UK's population and growth rate of labor input have been steadily declining, and the country has recently relaxed immigration policies to increase the labor participation rate. The labor input and total factor productivity data for the UK are given in Exhibit 2. Suzy forecasts economic growth through the growth accounting equation and the endogenous model.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1. Spot rate, forward points, and Libor
Exhibit 2. UK labor productivity and TFP (in %)

ECON-trump.title: Currency Trader -- Triangular Arbitrage, Parity and Policy
ECON-trump.background: A CFA candidate is studying currency exchange rates and consults a currency dealer who provides bid/offer quotes. The candidate examines a possible triangular arbitrage trade using the Swiss, US, and Brazilian currencies, based on a dealer's bid/offer quote of 0.2355/0.2358 in CHF/BRL and the interbank spot quotes in Exhibit 1. The candidate is also interested in interest rate parity and purchasing power parity and collects the data in Exhibit 2 for the GBP and CAD. The candidate asks about the effect on the exchange rate (Question 1): the government of Canada has decided to loosen its monetary policy and fiscal policy by expanding its monetary base and government spending to encourage private-sector investment; with high capital mobility and a flexible exchange rate regime, what impact will this have on the exchange rate? Finally, assessing Mexico, the candidate notes the central bank has recently liberalized financial markets and allowed foreign direct investment in select industries; Mexico's economic data are: growth due to capital deepening 1.7%, growth in labor productivity 3.4%, long-term growth rate of labor force 1.3%, growth in capital 6.2%, share of labor in GDP 40%.

questions.los: 内在价值 vs 市场价格, mispricing 两成分 (V-P 与感知误差)
questions.stem: 分析师估计的内在价值为 V_E，市场价格为 P，真实（不可观测）内在价值为 V。V_E − P 这一'表观错误定价'应如何分解？

choices.A: V_E − P 全部是可捕捉的 alpha——只要估值与价格不等，就存在真实错误定价
choices.B: V_E − P = (V − P) + (V_E − V)，即真实 mispricing 加上分析师自身的估值误差
choices.C: V_E − P 应分解为系统性风险溢价与流动性折价两部分

explanations.A: 错。把表观差价全当真实 mispricing，忽略了 V_E 本身可能估错。分析师看到的差价里混着自己的估值误差 (V_E − V)，这正是本 LOS 要打破的直觉。
explanations.B: 对。表观 mispricing = 真实 mispricing (V − P) + 估值误差 (V_E − V)。记法：'你看到的差价 = 市场错的 + 你错的'。只有前者才是可获利的来源，后者是你的风险。
explanations.C: 错。这是资产定价里的溢价分解语言，与 mispricing 分解无关——最易被'听起来专业'的表述带偏。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Equity Valuation: Applications and Processes, intrinsic value 与 mispricing 分解

questions.los: 绝对 vs 相对估值模型适用场景
questions.stem: 关于绝对估值 (absolute valuation) 与相对估值 (relative valuation) 模型，下列说法正确的是：

choices.A: DDM、FCF 模型、residual income 模型均为绝对估值模型，直接估计资产的内在价值
choices.B: Justified P/E 由 GGM 推导而来，因此属于纯相对估值，不依赖任何绝对模型假设
choices.C: 相对估值能够识别整个行业板块被系统性高估的情形

explanations.A: 对。绝对估值模型输出的是内在价值的具体估计（DDM/FCF/RI/asset-based 都是）；相对估值输出的是'相对于可比资产贵还是便宜'。记法：出'价值数字'的是绝对，出'贵/便宜排序'的是相对。
explanations.B: 错。justified multiple 恰恰是把绝对模型 (GGM) 的结论翻译成乘数形式，它的每个输入 (r, g, payout) 都来自绝对模型假设——这是'justified'与'comparables'两类乘数用法最易混淆之处。
explanations.C: 错。相对估值只能判断标的相对可比公司的高低估。若整个板块被高估，板块内'相对便宜'的股票仍可能绝对高估——这正是相对法的固有盲区。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Equity Valuation: Applications and Processes, 绝对与相对估值模型

questions.los: GGM: 公式、敏感性、隐含增长率/隐含要求回报
questions.stem: 某公司刚支付股利 D0 = 2.00，股利预期永续增长 g = 5%，要求回报率 r = 10%。用 GGM 计算的股票价值最接近：

explanations.A: 错。40.00 = 2.00/0.05，直接用了 D0 而没有先增长到 D1。GGM 分子永远是下一期股利 D1 = D0×(1+g)，'刚支付'三个字就是在提示 D0 需要乘 (1+g)。
explanations.B: 错。21.00 = 2.10/0.10，分母误用了 r 而不是 r − g。分母是'要求回报扣掉增长'——增长会抵消一部分折现。

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 题干给的是'刚支付'的 D0，必须先乘 (1+g)；分母是 r−g 不是 r。两个陷阱分别对应错误选项 40.00 与 21.00

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, Gordon growth model

questions.los: GGM: 公式、敏感性、隐含增长率/隐含要求回报
questions.stem: 某股票当前价格 P0 = 50，刚支付股利 D0 = 2.50，市场预期股利永续增长 g = 4%。若价格等于 GGM 价值，隐含的要求回报率 r 最接近：

explanations.B: 错。9.0% = 2.50/50 + 4%，用了 D0/P0 当股息率。反解 r 时分子同样必须是 D1——'刚支付'的 D0 要先乘 (1+g)，这个陷阱在正算和反解里完全一样。
explanations.C: 错。5.2% 只是 D1/P0（预期股息率），漏加了 g。GGM 的隐含回报由'现金收益 + 增长收益'两部分构成，只取一半是最常见的手滑。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: P0 = D1/(r−g) 反解得 r = D1/P0 + g

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 分子必须用 D1 而非 D0（否则得 9.0%）；股息率之外别忘加 g（否则得 5.2%）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, GGM 隐含要求回报

questions.los: 两阶段/H-model 计算与适用
questions.stem: D0 = 1.00，未来 2 年股利每年增长 20%，之后永续增长 5%，r = 10%。两阶段 DDM 下股票价值最接近：

explanations.A: 错。26.08 来自 TV2 = D2/(r−g) = 1.44/0.05 = 28.80——终值分子用了 D2 而没有让它再按 5% 增长到 D3。终值公式的分子永远是'终值时点的下一期股利'。
explanations.C: 错。25.00 是把 TV2 按 3 期折现 (30.24/1.10³) 得到的。TV2 是第 2 年末的价值，与 D2 同时点，只折 2 期——终值折现期数是两阶段模型的头号丢分点。

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: TV2 分子是 D3 不是 D2（错则得 26.08）；TV2 折 2 期不是 3 期（错则得 25.00）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, two-stage DDM

questions.los: 两阶段/H-model 计算与适用
questions.stem: D0 = 1.00，当前增长率 gS = 14%，预计在 8 年内线性下降至长期增长率 gL = 6% 并保持，r = 10%。用 H-model 计算的股票价值最接近：

explanations.B: 错。42.50 = (1.06 + 8×0.08)/0.04，把 H 用成了整个下降期 8 年。H-model 中 H = 下降期/2，因为线性下降的超额增长平均只享受一半时间。
explanations.C: 错。26.50 = 1.06/0.04，只算了长期 GGM 部分，漏掉了超额增长项 D0×H×(gS−gL)/(r−gL)。H-model 价值 = 长期 GGM 价值 + 超额增长附加值，两块缺一不可。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: V0 = [D0(1+gL) + D0 × H × (gS − gL)]/(r − gL)，H = 线性下降年数/2

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: H 取下降期的一半（用全长 8 得 42.50）；别漏超额增长项（漏则得 26.50）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, H-model

questions.los: PVGO 分解: E/r + PVGO
questions.stem: GGM 框架下，股票价格可分解为 P0 = E1/r + PVGO。关于该分解，下列说法正确的是：

choices.A: E1/r 假设公司将全部盈利再投资，因此代表'增长价值'
choices.B: PVGO 恒为正，因为增长总会创造价值
choices.C: E1/r 是 100% 分红、零增长下的价值；PVGO 可以为负——当再投资回报 ROE 低于 r 时增长毁灭价值

explanations.A: 错。方向完全反了：E1/r 是'no-growth value'，隐含 100% payout、零再投资、零增长。'全部再投资'对应的恰是 PVGO 那一块的来源。
explanations.B: 错。这是 PVGO 最重要的反直觉点：增长本身不创造价值，只有 ROE > r 的再投资才创造价值。ROE < r 时公司越扩张 PVGO 越负。
explanations.C: 对。P0 = E1/r（把全部盈利当永续股利折现的无增长价值）+ PVGO（增长机会现值）。记法：'先算躺平价值，再看增长是加分还是减分'——PVGO 的符号由 ROE 与 r 的大小关系决定。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, PVGO 分解

questions.los: SGR = b × ROE (与 PRAT 扩展)
questions.stem: 某公司 dividend payout ratio = 40%，ROE = 15%。其 sustainable growth rate (SGR) 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。6.0% = 0.40×15%，直接拿题干给的 payout ratio 乘了 ROE。SGR 用的是留存率 b = 1 − payout，题干故意给 payout 就是等你忘了做这一步转换。
explanations.B: 对。b = 1 − 0.40 = 0.60；SGR = b × ROE = 0.60 × 15% = 9.0%。口诀：'留下来的钱 × 钱生钱的速度'。看到 payout 先在旁边写 b = 1 − payout 再动笔。
explanations.C: 错。15.0% 是把 ROE 当成了 SGR，隐含假设公司零分红 (b=1)。只有全留存公司 SGR 才等于 ROE。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: SGR = b × ROE，b = 1 − dividend payout ratio

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 题干给 payout 不给 b——用 payout×ROE 得 6.0% 正是命题人埋的坑；忽略分红用 ROE 本身得 15.0% 同样是坑

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, sustainable growth rate

questions.los: GGM: 公式、敏感性、隐含增长率/隐含要求回报
questions.stem: 分析师对一只股票估计 D1 = 2.00、永续增长率 g = 12%、要求回报率 r = 10%，套用 GGM。正确的处理是：

choices.A: 照公式计算 2.00/(0.10−0.12) = −100，负值说明股票严重高估，应卖空
choices.C: GGM 在 g ≥ r 时失效，且 12% 的永续增长假设本身不合理——应改用多阶段模型，并把长期 g 压到不超过宏观经济长期增速

explanations.A: 错。负价格没有经济含义，它只说明模型假设被违反，不是'高估信号'。GGM 数学上要求 r > g 严格成立，g ≥ r 时公式发散、结果无效。
explanations.B: 错。对分母取绝对值没有任何理论依据，纯属'让数字能算出来'的数字游戏。模型假设错了，修数字不如修模型。
explanations.C: 对。两层问题都要看到：(1) 数学上 g ≥ r 使 GGM 失效；(2) 经济上没有公司能永续以 12% 增长——永续 g 的上限约为经济名义增速。高增长期该用两阶段或 H-model 处理。口诀：'g 贴近 r，价值上天；g 超过 r，换模型'。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Discounted Dividend Valuation, GGM 适用条件与敏感性

questions.los: FCFF from NI / EBIT / EBITDA / CFO 四条路径 (税调整差异)
questions.stem: EBIT = 200，利息费用 = 20，税率 = 25%，D&A = 40，FCInv = 60，WCInv = 20。FCFF 最接近：

explanations.A: 对。FCFF = EBIT×(1−t) + D&A − FCInv − WCInv = 200×0.75 + 40 − 60 − 20 = 110。EBIT 起步不需要碰利息——EBIT 本来就在利息之前。口诀：'EBIT 先交税，加折旧，减两投'。
explanations.B: 错。160 = 200 + 40 − 60 − 20，EBIT 忘了乘 (1−t)。四条路径里只有 NI 起步不用再对营业利润做税调整，EBIT/EBITDA 起步都必须先税后化。
explanations.C: 错。95 = 110 − 20×0.75，把税后利息又减了一遍。利息费用在这里是干扰信息：从 EBIT 出发利息还没被扣过，不存在'加回'或'再减'的问题——减税后利息是在算 FCFE 时才做的事。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: FCFF = EBIT(1−t) + D&A − FCInv − WCInv

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: EBIT 必须税后化（漏乘得 160）；利息是干扰项，EBIT 路径完全不涉及利息调整（多减税后利息得 95）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, FCFF from EBIT

questions.los: FCFF from NI / EBIT / EBITDA / CFO 四条路径 (税调整差异)
questions.stem: EBITDA = 150，D&A = 30，税率 = 30%，FCInv = 40，WCInv = 10。FCFF 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。55 = 150×0.70 − 50，漏掉了 +D&A×t 这一项。EBITDA 税后化时把 D&A 的抵税作用也'税掉'了，必须把折旧税盾 D&A×t 加回来。
explanations.B: 对。FCFF = EBITDA×(1−t) + D&A×t − FCInv − WCInv = 105 + 9 − 50 = 64。口诀：'EBITDA 路径只加回折旧的税盾（D&A×t），不是折旧本身'。
explanations.C: 错。85 = 105 + 30 − 50，把 D&A 全额加回了。全额加回是 EBIT 路径的动作（因为 EBIT 已扣除 D&A）；EBITDA 本来就没扣 D&A，只需要补它的税盾。两条路径的 D&A 处理差异是本 LOS 最核心的辨析点。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: FCFF = EBITDA(1−t) + D&A×t − FCInv − WCInv

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: EBITDA 路径加的是折旧税盾 D&A×t = 9，不是 D&A 全额 30（全额加回得 85，漏加税盾得 55）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, FCFF from EBITDA

questions.los: FCFE = FCFF − Int(1−t) + net borrowing
questions.stem: FCFF = 100，利息费用 = 20，税率 = 25%，当年新增借款 30、偿还借款 20（net borrowing = 10）。FCFE 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。90 = 100 − 20 + 10，减了全额利息没乘 (1−t)。从 FCFF 走向 FCFE 时扣的是税后利息——利息抵税省下的部分实际留在了股东口袋里。
explanations.B: 错。105 = 100 + 15 − 10，方向记反了：把税后利息加回、把净借款减掉。方向口诀：'股东要付利息（减），股东收到新借的钱（加）'。
explanations.C: 对。FCFE = FCFF − Int×(1−t) + net borrowing = 100 − 20×0.75 + 10 = 95。FCFE 是债权人拿走税后利息、借新还旧轧差之后归股东的现金流。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: FCFE = FCFF − Int×(1−t) + net borrowing

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 利息必须税后（全额减得 90）；净借款是加项、税后利息是减项，方向反了得 105

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, FCFF 与 FCFE 的关系

questions.los: 单阶段/两阶段 FCF 模型计算
questions.stem: 预期 FCFF1 = 60，WACC = 9%，股权要求回报 re = 12%，FCFF 永续增长 g = 4%。债务市值 = 400，流通股数 = 50。每股股权价值最接近：

explanations.A: 对。Firm value = FCFF1/(WACC−g) = 60/0.05 = 1200；Equity = 1200 − 400 = 800；每股 = 800/50 = 16.00。口诀：'FCFF 配 WACC，算完整体减债务'。
explanations.B: 错。24.00 = 1200/50，算出公司整体价值后直接除以股数，忘了减债务市值。FCFF 折出来的是全部资本提供者的价值，股东只分得扣除债务后的部分。
explanations.C: 错。7.00 来自用 re=12% 折 FCFF：60/(0.12−0.04) = 750，再减 400 除 50。折现率与现金流口径必须配对——FCFF 配 WACC，FCFE 才配 re。题干同时给出两个折现率就是考这一配对。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: Firm value = FCFF1/(WACC − g)；Equity value = Firm value − 债务市值；每股 = Equity/股数

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: FCFF 必须配 WACC（误配 re 得 7.00）；整体价值要先减债务再除股数（忘减得 24.00）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, 单阶段 FCFF 模型

questions.los: 何时 FCFF 优于 FCFE (资本结构不稳/FCFE为负)
questions.stem: 下列哪种情形下，用 FCFF 折现（再减去债务价值得到股权价值）比直接折现 FCFE 更合适？

choices.A: 公司股利支付稳定且与盈利能力挂钩
choices.B: 公司杠杆水平预计发生大幅变动，或 FCFE 当前为负
choices.C: 估值视角是无控制权的少数股东

explanations.A: 错。股利稳定且反映盈利能力时，DDM 就很合适，这不是选 FCFF 的理由——把'选 FCF 而非 DDM'的条件与'选 FCFF 而非 FCFE'的条件混在一起是常见错位。
explanations.B: 对。两大经典场景：(1) 资本结构剧变时，net borrowing 波动使 FCFE 极难预测，而 FCFF 不受融资决策干扰；(2) FCFE 为负时无法直接折现。记法：'借钱的事看不清，就退到 FCFF 这个融资前口径'。
explanations.C: 错。少数股东视角对应的是 DDM——小股东拿不到自由现金流的控制权，只能拿股利。FCF 模型本身隐含控制权视角。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, FCFF vs FCFE 模型选择

questions.los: FCFF from NI / EBIT / EBITDA / CFO 四条路径 (税调整差异)
questions.stem: 计算 FCFF/FCFE 时使用的 working capital investment (WCInv)，其营运资本口径正确的是：

choices.A: 直接使用资产负债表上流动资产减流动负债 (CA − CL) 的变动
choices.B: 排除现金及等价物，但应包含 notes payable 等短期有息负债
choices.C: 排除现金及等价物，同时排除 notes payable 与当期到期的长期债务等短期有息负债后的营运资本变动

explanations.A: 错。报表口径的 CA−CL 把现金和短期借款都卷了进来：现金是估值的结果不是营运投入，短期借款属于融资活动。直接用报表数是 WCInv 最常见的实务错误。
explanations.B: 错。只排除现金排了一半。Notes payable 与当期到期长债是融资项目，其变动属于 net borrowing（FCFE 里单独处理），混进 WCInv 会与融资现金流重复计算。
explanations.C: 对。估值用的营运资本 = (CA − cash) − (CL − 短期有息负债)。口诀：'掐头去尾——头上掐掉现金，尾上去掉有息'。留下的才是真正支撑经营的应收、存货、应付等项目。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, WCInv 的定义与口径

questions.los: FCFF from NI / EBIT / EBITDA / CFO 四条路径 (税调整差异)
questions.stem: CFO = 120（利息费用已在经营活动中扣除），利息费用 = 30，税率 = 25%，D&A = 25，FCInv = 50。FCFF 最接近：

explanations.A: 对。FCFF = CFO + Int×(1−t) − FCInv = 120 + 30×0.75 − 50 = 92.5。口诀：'CFO 路径最短——加税后利息，减固定投资，别的都别碰'。
explanations.B: 错。117.5 = 92.5 + 25，把 D&A 又加了一遍。CFO 是从 NI 加回非现金项目得来的，D&A 已经在 CFO 里面了——D&A 在此是纯干扰信息。同理 WCInv 也已含在 CFO 中，不能再减。
explanations.C: 错。100 = 120 + 30 − 50，利息全额加回没乘 (1−t)。加回税后利息的逻辑与 NI 路径一致：利息税盾的好处不归全部资本口径。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: FCFF = CFO + Int×(1−t) − FCInv（CFO 已含 NCC 与 WCInv）

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: D&A 与 WCInv 已在 CFO 中，再加/再减就是重复计算（加 D&A 得 117.5）；利息必须税后加回（全额得 100.0）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Free Cash Flow Valuation, FCFF from CFO

questions.los: Justified P/E (leading/trailing) 由 GGM 推导
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: 某公司 dividend payout ratio = 40%，ROE = 15%，要求回报率 r = 12%，增长率按 SGR 估计。justified leading P/E 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。14.53 = 0.40×1.09/0.03，套了 trailing P/E 公式 (1−b)(1+g)/(r−g)。题目问 leading（P0/E1），分子不乘 (1+g)。leading 和 trailing 只差一个 (1+g) 倍数，问哪个用哪个公式。
explanations.B: 对。g = b×ROE = 0.60×15% = 9%；justified leading P/E = (1−b)/(r−g) = 0.40/(0.12−0.09) = 13.33。口诀：'leading 配 E1，分子是 payout 原样；trailing 配 E0，分子多乘 (1+g)'。
explanations.C: 错。20.00 = 0.60/0.03，分子用了留存率 b 而不是 payout (1−b)。justified P/E 的分子是分红比例——P/E 由'分出来的那部分盈利'的折现支撑。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: g = b × ROE；justified leading P/E = P0/E1 = (1−b)/(r−g)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: leading 分子不乘 (1+g)（乘了就是 trailing 的 14.53）；分子是 payout 不是 b（用 b 得 20.00）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, justified leading P/E

questions.los: Justified P/E (leading/trailing) 由 GGM 推导
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: dividend payout ratio = 50%，g = 4%，r = 10%。分析师要与'基于最近四个季度已实现 EPS'计算的市场 P/E 作比较，应计算的 justified trailing P/E 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。8.33 = 0.50/0.06 是 leading P/E (P0/E1)。已实现 EPS 是 E0 口径，必须配 trailing 公式。题干'最近四个季度已实现'就是在指向 trailing——口径错了，与市场 P/E 的比较就差了 (1+g) 倍。
explanations.B: 错。17.33 = 1.04/0.06，漏乘了 payout ratio (1−b)。justified P/E 分子必须含分红比例，忘乘等于假设 100% 分红——P/E 由'分出来的那部分盈利'支撑，留存部分已经通过 g 体现在分母里了。
explanations.C: 对。justified trailing P/E = P0/E0 = (1−b)(1+g)/(r−g) = 0.50×1.04/0.06 = 8.67。口诀：'trailing 用旧盈利，旧盈利要长一岁——分子乘 (1+g)'。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: justified trailing P/E = P0/E0 = (1−b)(1+g)/(r−g)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 市场 P/E 用已实现 EPS（E0）时必须配 trailing 公式；套 leading 公式得 8.33，两者差 (1+g) 倍——leading/trailing 混用是乘数比较的头号错误

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, justified trailing P/E 与口径匹配

questions.los: P/B 与 ROE-r 关系; justified P/B = (ROE−g)/(r−g)
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: ROE = 16%，要求回报率 r = 12%，长期增长率 g = 6%。justified P/B 最接近：

explanations.A: 对。justified P/B = (ROE−g)/(r−g) = (0.16−0.06)/(0.12−0.06) = 0.10/0.06 = 1.67。口诀：'上下都减 g，上面是 ROE 下面是 r'。ROE > r 所以 P/B > 1，方向自检通过。
explanations.B: 错。0.67 = (ROE−r)/(r−g) = 0.04/0.06，分子误用了 ROE−r。(ROE−r) 出现在 RI 模型的超额收益项里，不是 justified P/B 的分子——两个公式长得像，最容易串。
explanations.C: 错。1.33 = ROE/r = 0.16/0.12，直接拿 ROE 除 r，完全丢掉了 g。这是'凭印象速算'的典型产物，g 在分子分母同时出现、不能约掉。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: justified P/B = (ROE − g)/(r − g)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 分子是 ROE−g 不是 ROE−r（后者得 0.67，与 RI 公式记串）；自检：ROE>r 时 P/B 必须大于 1

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, justified P/B

questions.los: P/B 与 ROE-r 关系; justified P/B = (ROE−g)/(r−g)
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: 基于 justified P/B = (ROE−g)/(r−g)，下列说法正确的是：

choices.A: 提高增长率 g 总会提高 justified P/B
choices.B: ROE > r 时 justified P/B > 1，且此时 g 越高 P/B 越高；ROE < r 时提高 g 反而压低 P/B

explanations.A: 错。g 的作用方向取决于 ROE 与 r 的关系：ROE < r 时公司每留存一元都在毁灭价值，g 越高 P/B 越低。'增长必然抬估值'是需要被这个公式纠正的直觉。
explanations.B: 对。P/B 与 1 的大小关系完全由 ROE−r 的符号决定，g 只是放大器：赚超额收益时放大向上，亏超额收益时放大向下。口诀：'ROE 对 r，定方向；g 定力度'。
explanations.C: 错。ROE = r 时分子分母同为 (r−g)，P/B = 1 而不是 0——赚的恰好是要求回报，市场只愿意按账面价值定价。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, P/B 与 ROE−r 的关系

questions.los: EV/EBITDA 适用场景与陷阱
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: 关于 EV/EBITDA 乘数，下列说法正确的是：

choices.A: EV = 股权市值 + 债务市值，不需要扣减现金及等价物
choices.B: EBITDA 已反映公司间资本密集度差异，因此重资产公司之间可直接比较
choices.C: 适合比较资本结构差异较大的公司，且净利润为负时 EBITDA 往往仍为正、乘数仍可用

explanations.A: 错。EV = 股权市值 + 债务市值 + 优先股 + 少数股东权益 − 现金及等价物。减现金是因为收购方可用目标公司自己的现金抵减收购成本——漏减现金是 EV 计算的第一大错。
explanations.B: 错。恰恰相反：EBITDA 在折旧摊销之前，完全没有反映维持性资本开支的差异。资本密集度不同的公司比 EV/EBITDA 会系统性误导——这是 EBITDA 乘数最重要的陷阱。
explanations.C: 对。EV 是全部资本口径、EBITDA 是利息之前的利润口径，上下匹配，天然中和了杠杆差异；且 EBITDA 为负比 EPS 为负少见得多。口诀：'比杠杆不同的公司，上 EV 口径；但别忘了它看不见 capex'。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, EV/EBITDA 的适用与局限

questions.los: PEG 的用法与缺陷
questions.module: Market-Based Valuation: Price and Enterprise Value Multiples
questions.stem: 分析师声称：'PEG 更低的股票一定比 PEG 更高的股票更被低估。'该说法最主要的问题是：

choices.A: PEG 隐含 P/E 与 g 之间的线性关系，且未对风险差异和增长可持续期进行调整
choices.B: PEG 只能用 trailing P/E 计算，用 leading P/E 计算会使结论无效
choices.C: PEG 只适用于增长率为负的公司

explanations.A: 对。PEG 的三大缺陷：(1) 假设 P/E 与 g 线性成比例，而 GGM 推导下这一关系是非线性的；(2) 不反映风险——高风险高增长股 PEG 低但未必便宜；(3) 不区分增长的持续期与质量。口诀：'PEG 只除了一个 g，风险和久期它都没除'。
explanations.B: 错。PEG 用 leading 或 trailing P/E 都可以，关键是可比公司之间口径一致。口径问题是使用规范，不是 PEG 的固有缺陷——拿'规范'当'缺陷'是干扰项的经典造法。
explanations.C: 错。方向说反了：g ≤ 0 时 PEG 失去意义（负 PEG 无法排序），PEG 恰恰只在正增长公司之间才可用。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Market-Based Valuation, PEG ratio 的缺陷

questions.los: 单阶段 RI 模型: V0 = BV0 + (ROE−r)×BV0/(r−g)
questions.stem: 每股期初账面价值 BV0 = 20，长期 ROE = 14%，股权要求回报 r = 10%，RI 永续增长 g = 6%。单阶段 RI 模型下每股价值最接近：

explanations.A: 错。60 = 20 + (0.14−0.06)×20/0.04，超额收益项的分子误用了 ROE−g。分子必须是 ROE−r（超额于股东要求回报的部分），g 只出现在分母——与 justified P/B 公式记串的镜像错误。
explanations.C: 错。20 只是 (ROE−r)×BV0/(r−g) = 20 或 BV0 本身——漏掉了另一半。RI 估值 = 账面价值 + 超额收益现值，两块都要，只写一块正好丢一半价值。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: V0 = BV0 + (ROE − r)×BV0/(r − g)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 分子是 ROE−r 不是 ROE−g（后者得 60）；别忘了 BV0 打底（漏加得 20）

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Residual Income Valuation, 单阶段 RI 模型

questions.los: Persistence factor ω 的含义与取值影响
questions.stem: 每股 BV0 = 10，预期明年 RI1 = 1.50，此后 RI 每年按 persistence factor ω = 0.60 衰减，r = 10%。RI 模型下每股价值最接近：

explanations.A: 错。25.00 = 10 + 1.50/0.10，把 RI 当成了不衰减的永续年金（相当于 ω=1）。ω<1 表示竞争会侵蚀超额收益，衰减效应必须体现在分母里。
explanations.B: 错。3.00 只是 RI 现值 1.50/(1+0.10−0.60)，漏加了 BV0。RI 模型的价值锚是账面价值，超额收益现值只是加层。
explanations.C: 对。衰减 RI 的现值 = RI1/(1+r−ω) = 1.50/(1.10−0.60) = 3.00；V0 = BV0 + 3.00 = 13.00。ω 的两个极端：ω=1 → RI 永续（除以 r）；ω=0 → RI 一期后归零。口诀：'ω 越大，超额收益越长寿，价值越高'。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: 衰减 RI 现值 = RI1/(1 + r − ω)；V0 = BV0 + RI1/(1 + r − ω)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: ω=0.6 时分母是 1+r−ω=0.50，不能按永续年金除以 r（得 25.00）；BV0 是价值锚，漏加得 3.00

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Residual Income Valuation, persistence factor 与 continuing RI

questions.los: Clean surplus 假设及其违反的后果
questions.stem: RI 模型依赖 clean surplus 关系：BV1 = BV0 + NI − dividends。下列哪一项会违反该关系？

choices.A: 外币报表折算差额 (CTA) 绕过利润表直接计入 OCI
choices.C: 公司计提折旧与摊销费用

explanations.A: 对。Clean surplus 要求所有影响账面权益的损益都先经过 NI。CTA、FVOCI 证券公允价值变动、养老金重估等直接进 OCI 的项目让权益变了而 NI 没变——账面'不干净'了，用报表 NI 算 RI 会系统性偏差，需调整或改用综合收益。
explanations.B: 错。股利本来就是 clean surplus 关系式中的一项 (−dividends)，与股东的资本交易不构成违反。把'绕过利润表的损益'和'与股东的交易'混为一谈是本考点最常见的错误。
explanations.C: 错。D&A 完整地经过利润表进入 NI，是最'干净'的项目，与 clean surplus 无冲突。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Residual Income Valuation, clean surplus 假设的违反

questions.los: RI vs DDM/FCF 适用场景
questions.stem: 相比 DDM 与 FCF 模型，residual income 模型最适合下列哪种公司？

choices.A: 频繁通过 OCI 确认大额损益、会计透明度低的公司
choices.B: 不支付股利、预期未来多年 FCF 为负，但账面价值与 ROE 可较可靠预测的公司
choices.C: 价值主要集中在远期终值的高成长早期公司——因为 RI 模型对终值的依赖最大

explanations.A: 错。大量损益绕道 OCI 恰恰破坏 clean surplus 假设，是 RI 模型的软肋而非用武之地。RI 依赖会计数据质量，会计越'脏'越难用。
explanations.B: 对。RI 的经典适用场景：不分红（DDM 失效）、FCF 长期为负（FCF 模型难用），只要 BV 与 ROE 可预测，RI 依然能落地。口诀：'没股利没现金流，还有账面价值可依靠'。
explanations.C: 错。方向反了：RI 模型的价值大头由当期 BV0 与近期超额收益构成，对终值的依赖比 DDM/FCF 小——这正是 RI 的优点之一，干扰项把优点说成了缺点再倒扣回来。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Residual Income Valuation, RI 模型适用场景

questions.los: RI = NI − re×BV0 = (ROE−re)×BV0
questions.stem: 期初账面权益 BV0 = 100，当期 NI = 20，当期未支付股利也无其他权益变动，故期末账面权益 BV1 = 120。股权成本 re = 10%。当期 residual income 最接近：

explanations.A: 错。8.0 = 20 − 0.10×120，equity charge 用了期末 BV1。期末权益里包含了当期利润本身，用它计费等于'让当年赚的钱为自己付资本成本'。题干给出 BV1 就是等你选错时点。
explanations.B: 错。9.0 = 20 − 0.10×110，用了平均 BV。平均口径是某些 ROE 计算的惯例，但 RI 的 equity charge 明确基于期初投入的资本——年初股东放进去多少钱，就按多少钱收要求回报。
explanations.C: 对。RI = NI − re×BV0 = 20 − 0.10×100 = 10.0。口诀：'资本费用按年初的本钱算'——equity charge 是对期初已投入资本的机会成本。等价写法：RI = (ROE−re)×BV0 = (0.20−0.10)×100 = 10。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: RI = NI − re × BV0（期初账面权益）

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: equity charge 基于期初 BV0=100；用期末 120 得 8.0、用平均 110 得 9.0，题干给出 BV1 就是干扰项

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Residual Income Valuation, RI 定义与 equity charge

questions.los: DLOC 与 DLOM 的叠加计算: 总折扣 = 1−(1−DLOC)(1−DLOM)
questions.stem: 某私营公司按控股、可流通基础估出的每股价值为 100 元。对一笔少数股权、无流通性的股份，适用 DLOC = 20%、DLOM = 25%。该笔股份的每股价值最接近：

explanations.B: 错。55 = 100×(1−0.20−0.25)，把两个折扣直接相加成 45%。加法夸大了总折扣（45% > 40%），因为第二重折扣的基数已经变小了——这是 DLOC/DLOM 唯一但必考的陷阱。
explanations.C: 错。75 = 100×(1−0.25)，只应用了 DLOM 而忽略 DLOC。少数股权 + 缺乏流通性是两项独立缺陷，都要扣：先因'管不了'打折，再因'卖不掉'打折。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: 价值 = 基准价值 × (1 − DLOC) × (1 − DLOM)；总折扣 = 1 − (1−DLOC)(1−DLOM)

steps.label: 结果
steps.content: 价值 = 60 元（总折扣 40%）

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 两折扣是乘法叠加，直接相加 45% 得 55 元是最常见错误；只用其中一个折扣得 75 元

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Private Company Valuation, DLOC 与 DLOM 的叠加

questions.los: 三种方法: income / market / asset-based
questions.stem: 私营公司估值中，excess earnings method 与 guideline transactions method 分别属于哪类方法？

explanations.A: 错。两者正好颠倒。记分类看'价值从哪来'：excess earnings 是把无形资产的超额盈利资本化——盈利折现，属 income；guideline transactions 用可比公司整体收购交易的乘数——比价，属 market。
explanations.B: 对。Income approach 三件套：FCF 法、capitalized cash flow method、excess earnings method；market approach 三件套：guideline public company (GPCM)、guideline transactions (GTM)、prior transactions。口诀：'折现归 income，比价归 market，清点家底归 asset-based'。
explanations.C: 错。Excess earnings method 虽然要先给营运资本和固定资产分配回报，但其核心是把剩余盈利资本化为无形资产价值，课纲将其归入 income approach 而非 asset-based。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Private Company Valuation, 三大估值方法分类

questions.los: CAPM 扩展: build-up method, expanded CAPM
questions.stem: 用 build-up method 估计私营公司股权要求回报率时，与 expanded CAPM 相比的关键区别是：

choices.A: build-up method 用行业 beta 乘以股权风险溢价后，再加 size premium
choices.B: expanded CAPM 不包含 size premium 与 company-specific premium
choices.C: build-up method 不使用 beta（相当于 beta 取 1），在无风险利率上直接叠加 ERP、size premium 与 company-specific premium

explanations.A: 错。'beta × ERP 再加溢价'描述的是 expanded CAPM 的结构。build-up 之所以叫'堆叠法'，就是因为它放弃了 beta 估计——把两种方法的定义互换是本考点的标准干扰项造法。
explanations.B: 错。恰恰相反：expanded CAPM = rf + beta×ERP + size premium + company-specific premium，'expanded'扩的就是这两个溢价。没有这两项的是普通 CAPM。
explanations.C: 对。私营公司没有市场价格序列可估 beta，build-up method 直接令 beta = 1：r = rf + ERP + size premium + industry premium + company-specific premium。口诀：'估不出 beta 就不用 beta，全靠往上堆溢价'。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Private Company Valuation, build-up method 与 expanded CAPM

questions.los: Spot/forward/par 曲线关系; forward rate model 计算
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 1 年期 spot rate S1 = 3%，2 年期 spot rate S2 = 4%（年复利）。1 年后起算的 1 年期 forward rate f(1,1) 最接近：

explanations.A: 对。(1+S2)^2 = (1+S1)(1+f(1,1))，f(1,1) = 1.04^2/1.03 − 1 = 1.0816/1.03 − 1 = 5.01%。记法：长端整体收益 = 短端收益 × forward 收益，'长的除以短的'。曲线上行时 forward 必然高于长端 spot（4%），可用此方向感先排除 B、C。
explanations.B: 错。0.97% = 1.04/1.03 − 1，两个 spot rate 都忘了配期数（没有对 S2 平方）。forward rate model 的每一项都是'总回报因子'，必须带上各自的期数次方。
explanations.C: 错。2.01% = 1.03^2/1.04 − 1，把分子分母的期数用反了——短期限放到了平方位置。检查方法：上行曲线下 forward 必须 > S2，2.01% < 4% 直接矛盾。

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 期数次方最易错：分子用长期限的次方、分母用短期限的次方。快速校验：上行曲线下 f(1,1) 应高于 S2 = 4%。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, forward rate model

questions.los: Spot/forward/par 曲线关系; forward rate model 计算
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 2 年期 spot rate S2 = 4%，3 年期 spot rate S3 = 5%（年复利）。2 年后起算的 1 年期 forward rate f(2,1) 最接近：

explanations.B: 错。6.01% = 1.05^2/1.04 − 1，期数用错——把 S3 只配了 2 次方、S2 配了 1 次方，等于把 f(2,1) 算成了 f(1,1) 的结构。forward 记号 f(a,b) 中 a 是起点，分母必须是 (1+Sa)^a。
explanations.C: 错。4.50% 是两个 spot rate 的简单平均。spot 是 forward 的'几何平均'结果，反解 forward 从来不是对 spot 取平均——这是完全绕开 forward rate model 的想当然算法。

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 分子分母各自的次方必须等于各自的期限（3 和 2）。近似检验：3×5% − 2×4% = 7%，与精确值 7.03% 接近即算对了。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, forward rate model

questions.los: Spot/forward/par 曲线关系; forward rate model 计算
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 收益率曲线向上倾斜（upward-sloping）时，同一期限上 par rate、spot rate、forward rate 的大小排序为：

explanations.A: 对。上行曲线时：spot 是此前各期 forward 的几何平均，平均值必然低于末端最高的 forward，故 forward > spot；par rate 是用整条 spot 曲线折现的'混合利率'，掺入了较低的短端 spot，故 spot > par。记法：曲线上行时'forward 在最上、par 在最下'，曲线下行时整体反过来。
explanations.B: 错。spot > forward 只在曲线向下倾斜时成立。spot 是 forward 的几何平均——平均数不可能高于推动它上升的边际数（forward）。
explanations.C: 错。这是下行（inverted）曲线的排序。若把'par 由 spot 平均而来、spot 由 forward 平均而来'的层级记反，就会得到这个完全颠倒的答案。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, par/spot/forward curve relationships

questions.los: Riding the yield curve 策略条件
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 投资期限为 1 年的投资者采用 riding the yield curve（rolling down the yield curve）策略获取超额回报，需要满足的条件是：

choices.A: 收益率曲线向上倾斜且预期在持有期内保持不变，买入期限长于 1 年的债券
choices.B: 预期利率将上升，买入期限恰好等于 1 年的债券锁定收益
choices.C: 收益率曲线向上倾斜，买入期限短于 1 年的债券以降低久期风险

explanations.A: 对。策略本质：曲线上行且静止时，长债随时间'滑向'更低收益率的短端，收益率下滑带来价格上升，持有回报高于直接买 1 年期债。两个条件缺一不可：曲线上行 + 曲线不动（即未来 spot 低于当前 forward 隐含的水平）。
explanations.B: 错。买期限恰好匹配投资期的债券是'免疫/锁定'做法，恰恰是 riding 策略要战胜的基准；且该策略赌的是利率不升（不实现 forward 隐含的上升），预期利率上升时不应使用。
explanations.C: 错。买短于持有期的债券会产生再投资缺口，且短债无法享受'滑下曲线'的价格增值——riding 的收益来源就是持有长于投资期的债券。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, riding the yield curve

questions.los: 利率期限结构理论 (纯预期/流动性偏好/市场分割等)
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 在 liquidity preference theory（流动性偏好理论）下，向上倾斜的收益率曲线意味着：

choices.A: 不一定意味着市场预期短期利率上升——即使预期利率不变甚至小幅下降，流动性溢价也可能使曲线上行
choices.B: 市场一定预期未来短期利率上升
choices.C: 长短期债券市场彼此分割，各自的供需独立决定利率

explanations.A: 对。流动性偏好理论 = 预期 + 随期限递增的流动性溢价。上行曲线可能全部来自溢价，无法单独反推利率预期。记法：'加了溢价的曲线，读不出纯预期'。
explanations.B: 错。这是 unbiased/pure expectations theory 的推论——该理论假设无风险溢价，forward rate 就是预期未来 spot rate 的无偏估计。把两个理论的结论套用混了。
explanations.C: 错。这是 segmented markets theory 的主张，与流动性偏好理论无关。市场分割理论下曲线形状由各期限区间各自的供需决定，不涉及统一的溢价结构。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, term structure theories

questions.los: Swap spread, Z-spread, TED spread 含义
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 市场数据：3 个月 Libor（MRR）= 2.10%，3 个月 T-bill 收益率 = 1.60%，2 年期 swap rate = 2.80%，2 年期国债收益率 = 2.45%。TED spread 为：

explanations.A: 对。TED spread = 3 个月 Libor − 3 个月 T-bill = 2.10% − 1.60% = 0.50%。它衡量银行间市场相对政府信用的短期信用/流动性风险。记法：T(-bill) 与 ED（欧洲美元期货代码）之差，全部在 3 个月短端。
explanations.B: 错。0.35% = 2.80% − 2.45% 是 swap spread（同期限 swap rate 减国债收益率）。swap spread 在任意期限上定义，TED 专指 3 个月短端两个具体品种之差，二者最易混淆。
explanations.C: 错。0.70% = 2.80% − 2.10% 是拿 2 年 swap rate 减 3 个月 Libor，期限错配的无意义组合——TED 的两条腿必须同为 3 个月期限。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: TED spread = 3 个月 Libor(MRR) − 3 个月 T-bill 收益率

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 不要抓到两个利率就相减：swap spread 用同期限 swap 与国债，TED 只用 3 个月 Libor 与 3 个月 T-bill。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, swap spread / TED spread

questions.los: Key rate duration 与曲线形变管理
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 一只 10 年期零息国债，其 key rate duration 的分布特征是：

choices.A: 几乎全部集中在 10 年期这一个关键期限点上，其他期限点的 key rate duration 约为零
choices.B: 在各关键期限点上大致均匀分布，因为总久期约为 10
choices.C: 集中在短端，因为短端利率波动最频繁

explanations.A: 对。零息债只有到期日一笔现金流，只有 10 年期 spot rate 的变动影响其价格，故 key rate duration 集中于 10 年点。记法：key rate duration 跟着'现金流落点'走，零息债现金流只落在到期日。
explanations.B: 错。这是把 effective duration（对整条曲线平移的敏感度）错误地'摊'到各期限点。总久期高不代表对每个期限点都敏感——付息债的 KRD 才会分散在各现金流日期上。
explanations.C: 错。混淆了'利率波动的频率'与'价格对该点利率的敏感度'。KRD 度量的是后者：某点利率即使天天波动，只要该点没有现金流折现暴露，KRD 依然为零。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, key rate duration

questions.los: Spot/forward/par 曲线关系; forward rate model 计算
questions.module: The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics
questions.stem: 若未来各期 spot rate 的实际走势恰好等于当前 forward 曲线隐含的水平，则在同一持有期内，持有长期债券相对滚动持有短期债券的超额回报为：

choices.A: 零——所有期限策略实现相同的持有期回报
choices.B: 为正——曲线上行时长债票息更高，必然跑赢
choices.C: 为负——长债久期更大，利率上升时亏损更多

explanations.A: 对。forward rate 是盈亏平衡（breakeven）利率：当未来 spot 恰好按 forward 实现时，任何期限的债券在同一持有期内回报相同。riding the yield curve 之所以能赚钱，赌的正是'未来 spot 低于 forward 隐含水平'。
explanations.B: 错。这是最常见的直觉陷阱：曲线上行 ≠ 长债必赢。若利率按 forward 隐含路径上升，长债的资本损失会恰好抵消其更高的收益率，超额回报归零——forward 定价已经把'更高票息'的好处对冲掉了。
explanations.C: 错。方向同样不对。利率虽按 forward 路径上升，但这个上升幅度恰好是市场定价好的盈亏平衡点，久期损失被期初更高的收益率精确补偿，不会为负。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Term Structure and Interest Rate Dynamics, forward rates as breakeven rates

questions.los: Binomial tree: backward induction 定价
questions.stem: 2 年期年付息债券，票面利率 4%，面值 100。二叉树利率（各节点为未来 1 年利率，风险中性概率各 0.5）：t=0 节点 3.0%；t=1 上节点 4.5%，下节点 3.5%。用 backward induction 计算债券当前价值最接近：

explanations.B: 错。97.09 = 0.5×(99.52+100.48)/1.03，折回 t=0 时漏加了 t=1 收到的票息 4。backward induction 每退一步，分子里都是'下期节点值 + 下期现金流'，漏 coupon 是本考点第一大失分点。
explanations.C: 错。104.00 = 0.5×(103.52+104.48)，算出了 t=1 的期望现金流总额却忘了用 t=0 利率 3% 折现回来。树上每退一层必须除以该节点的 1+r。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: 每个节点：V = 0.5×[(Vu + C) + (Vd + C)] / (1 + r节点)；末期现金流 = 面值 + 票息 = 104

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 两个高频错误：折回时漏加当期票息（得 97.09）、最后一步忘折现（得 104.00）。每退一层自查：加票息了吗？除以 1+r 了吗？

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, backward induction

questions.los: Binomial tree: backward induction 定价
questions.stem: 年付息 3% 的债券，二叉树 t=1 两个节点的债券价值（不含当期票息）分别为：上节点 98.80，下节点 100.50，概率各 0.5。t=0 的 1 年利率为 2.5%。债券在 t=0 的价值最接近：

explanations.B: 错。97.22 = 0.5×(98.80+100.50)/1.025，直接把两个除息节点值平均后折现，漏掉了 t=1 的票息 3。题干特意注明'不含当期票息'就是提示你要自己加回去。
explanations.C: 错。102.65 = 0.5×(101.80+103.50)，票息加对了却没有除以 1.025 折现。把'期望现金流'当成了'现值'——backward induction 的 backward 就体现在每层折现上。

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 题目给的节点值若注明'不含票息'（ex-coupon），折回时必须加票息；若给的是'含票息全价'则不能重复加。审题先确认口径。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, backward induction

questions.los: Tree 校准与利率波动率的关系 (相邻节点 ×e^{2σ})
questions.stem: 对数正态二叉利率树中，某期下节点利率为 3.00%，假设利率波动率 σ = 15%。同期相邻上节点的利率最接近：

explanations.A: 对。同一期相邻节点满足 r_u = r_d × e^{2σ} = 3.00% × e^{0.30} = 3.00% × 1.3499 ≈ 4.05%。记法：上下节点差两个'波动率台阶'（各偏离中值 e^{±σ}），所以相邻节点之间是 e^{2σ}。
explanations.B: 错。3.49% = 3.00% × e^{0.15}，只乘了 e^{σ}。e^{σ} 是节点相对'中间值'的单边偏移，相邻两个节点之间相差的是两倍指数 e^{2σ}——'2'漏掉是本公式最典型的错误。
explanations.C: 错。3.90% = 3.00% × (1 + 2×0.15)，用线性近似替代了指数。σ 较大时线性近似误差明显，曲线校准必须用精确的 e^{2σ}，考试给的选项就是用来区分这两种算法的。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: 对数正态树同期相邻节点：r_u = r_d × e^{2σ}

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 指数是 2σ 不是 σ；且是乘 e^{2σ} 而非加 2σ。若给出隔两档的节点（相隔 2 格），则相差 e^{4σ}，以此类推。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, interest rate tree calibration

questions.los: Tree 校准与利率波动率的关系 (相邻节点 ×e^{2σ})
questions.stem: 构建 arbitrage-free 二叉利率树时，'校准 (calibration)' 的直接目标是：

choices.A: 在给定波动率假设下调整各期节点利率，使树对基准债券（benchmark bonds）的定价与其市场价格一致
choices.B: 调整节点利率使其等于历史利率的实际路径
choices.C: 调整波动率假设使所有节点利率等于对应的 forward rate

explanations.A: 对。arbitrage-free 的含义就是'树能复现当前市场'：给定 σ，反复调节各期利率水平（同期节点保持 e^{2σ} 间隔），直到基准国债/par 曲线上的债券被树定价为其市场价。之后才能用这棵树给含权债定价。
explanations.B: 错。校准面向当前市场价格（无套利），与历史利率路径无关。用历史数据估计的是统计模型，不是 arbitrage-free 框架的做法。
explanations.C: 错。因果颠倒：波动率是外生输入假设，不是校准对象；且只有当 σ=0 时树的中间路径才退化为 forward rate，正常校准下节点利率围绕 forward 隐含水平上下展开。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, tree calibration

questions.los: Pathwise valuation 与 Monte Carlo 适用场景
questions.stem: 对 MBS（mortgage-backed securities）估值时，必须使用 Monte Carlo 模拟而非二叉树 backward induction 的根本原因是：

choices.A: MBS 现金流具有路径依赖性——提前还款取决于利率走过的历史路径，而 backward induction 中每个节点无法记住到达该节点的路径
choices.B: MBS 期限太长，二叉树节点数量会超出计算能力
choices.C: Monte Carlo 不需要利率波动率假设，比二叉树更客观

explanations.A: 对。提前还款行为受'利率是否曾经低过'（burnout 效应）等历史信息影响，同一节点经不同路径到达时现金流不同。backward induction 从后往前推，节点值与路径无关，天然处理不了路径依赖；Monte Carlo 沿每条模拟路径从前往后算现金流，正好解决。
explanations.B: 错。节点数量是计算量问题不是原理问题——递归组合树的节点数随期数线性/平方增长，完全可算。二叉树失效的原因是'无法携带路径信息'这一结构性缺陷。
explanations.C: 错。Monte Carlo 同样需要利率过程与波动率假设（还要加上提前还款模型），并不更'客观'。callable/putable 债券的行权只看当期利率与价格（非路径依赖），所以用 backward induction 即可，不必上 Monte Carlo。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, Monte Carlo / pathwise valuation

questions.los: Binomial tree: backward induction 定价
questions.stem: 用校准好的二叉利率树给一只不含权（option-free）债券定价，并与直接用当前 spot 曲线折现现金流的结果比较，二者关系是：

choices.A: 必然相等，且与树采用的波动率假设无关
choices.B: 波动率假设越高，树上得到的价值越低
choices.C: 树上价值系统性高于 spot 曲线折现值，因为树包含了利率上行情景

explanations.A: 对。校准的定义就是让树复现基准（spot/par）曲线定价。不含权债券现金流固定，无论 σ 取多少，校准过程都会把节点利率调整到使其定价回到 spot 折现值——波动率只影响含权债券（改变期权价值），不影响无权债。
explanations.B: 错。这是把'波动率↑使 callable 价值↓'的结论错误外推到无权债。波动率升高时校准会同步压低/调整节点利率使基准定价不变，无权债价值不动；受影响的只是嵌入期权部分。
explanations.C: 错。树的上行情景与下行情景围绕校准中枢对称展开（风险中性概率各 0.5），期望折现值不会系统性偏高。若树给无权债定出与 spot 折现不同的价，说明树没校准好，存在套利。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, The Arbitrage-Free Valuation Framework, arbitrage-free property of calibrated trees

questions.los: V_call = V_straight − V_callable; V_put 类似
questions.module: Valuation and Analysis of Bonds with Embedded Options
questions.stem: 2 年期年付息 4.5% 债券，面值 100，发行人可在 t=1 付息后按 100 赎回。二叉树利率（概率各 0.5）：t=0 为 3.5%；t=1 上节点 5.0%，下节点 3.0%。该 callable bond 当前价值最接近：

explanations.B: 错。101.44 是不施加赎回规则的 straight bond 价值（下节点保留 101.46）。忘记在节点上执行 min(V, call price) 检查，算出的就是无权债——二者之差 0.70 恰是嵌入 call 的价值。
explanations.C: 错。96.62 是把'节点值+票息'与赎回价比较（min(104.02,100)=100、min(105.96,100)=100）后折现的结果。赎回比较只针对债券的除息延续价值，票息归持有人所有，不参与与 call price 的比较。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: 含权节点值 = min(V节点, call price)；V节点 = 剩余现金流/(1+r节点)；折回时 V0 = 0.5×[(V'u+C)+(V'd+C)]/(1+r0)

steps.label: 陷阱
steps.content: 只在低利率（价格高）节点才会触发赎回；与 call price 比较的是除息节点值，不含当期票息。忘记赎回规则得 101.44（straight 价值）。

questions.source: CFA L2 Curriculum, Valuation and Analysis of Bonds with Embedded Options, callable bond valuation with binomial tree

questions.los: V_call = V_straight − V_callable; V_put 类似
questions.module: Valuation and Analysis of Bonds with Embedded Options
questions.stem: 同一发行人、同期限同票息的三只债券估值：不含权债券 102.5，callable 债券 99.8，putable 债券 104.0。嵌入 put option 的价值为：

explanations.A: 对。V_put = V_putable − V_straight = 104.0 − 102.5 = 1.5。put 在投资者手里，是'加分项'：V_putable = V_straight + V_put。记法：'put 加 call 减'——putable 比 straight 贵、callable 比 straight 便宜。
explanations.B: 错。2.7 = 102.5 − 99.8 = V_straight − V_callable，这算出来的是 call option 的价值，答非所问。call 与 put 的价值方程方向相反，审题先确认问的是哪个期权。
explanations.C: 错。4.2 = 104.0 − 99.8，拿 putable 直接减 callable，把 callable 当成了 straight 基准。这个差值是'put 价值 + call 价值'的混合，单独不代表任何一个期权。

steps.label: 公式
steps.content: V_putable = V_straight + V_put，故 V_put = V_putable − V_straight

steps.label: 陷阱
